title: Tamsin and the Scholarship
premise: Dominic Eastwick has spent her whole life being careful — the scholarship kid at a wealthy school, the baker's daughter who kneads her feelings into loaves instead of saying them aloud. When a group chat of classmates starts predicting events days before they happen, Dominic realizes she's the only one who can't see the future... and that the predictions are converging on her. To survive what's coming, she must win the baking championship everyone expects her to lose and confess the truth about who she really is before prom night, when the final prediction comes due. In the end, Dominic learns that belonging was never something to be earned — it's something she has to claim for herself.
about_author: Petra Almeida is a former pastry chef who traded early-morning shifts in a Lisbon bakery for late nights writing stories about kids who feel too much. She lives with a sourdough starter named after her grandmother.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. We meet her at 4 a.m. in the family bakery, folding anxiety into dough before another day of pretending she belongs at Ashford Academy on scholarship. A careless comment from a rich classmate stings; she swallows it, as always. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Group Chat Nobody Made
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. An unknown group chat adds her and predicts a fire drill two days early — it happens exactly as described. Her lab partner Priya admits she's been getting predictions too. Emotional beat: the first crack in Dominic's careful, controlled world.

chapters.title: What the Bread Knows
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The predictions turn personal: one names Dominic by initial. Meanwhile Dominic bakes through panic, and her bread comes out tasting like fear — customers notice. Emotional beat: terror that her inner life is visible to everyone.

chapters.title: Entry Fee
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The regional baking championship offers a full-ride scholarship to the winner — her only escape route if things collapse. But entering means competing publicly against classmates who already resent her. Emotional beat: hope tangled with exposure.

chapters.title: Predictions With Teeth
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A prediction foretells an accident in the school kitchen; Dominic ignores it to protect her entry, and someone gets hurt — not fatally, but badly. Guilt lands hard. Emotional beat: the price of survival starts coming due.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Yearbook
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Digging into the chat's origin, she finds a photo of a student who died at Ashford twenty years ago — a baker's kid, just like her. The predictions may be warnings, not threats. Emotional beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Quarterfinals
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the championship quarterfinals, sabotage ruins her first bake; she improvises with what the bakery taught her and advances anyway. Priya decodes the chat's pattern: every prediction protects someone who refuses to ask for help. Emotional beat: defiance.

chapters.title: Prom Is a Prediction
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The final message arrives: 'At prom, the Eastwick girl stops hiding or stops.' Dominic plans to skip prom entirely; her friends refuse to let her disappear. Emotional beat: chosen family versus self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She wins the finals — and realizes mid-ceremony that the trophy changes nothing about what prom holds. She leaves the stage early, flour still on her cuffs, to face the real contest. Emotional beat: clarity over validation.

chapters.title: Risen
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, closing with Priya. At prom, Dominic stands before the school and tells the truth — about the scholarship, the fear, the dead girl who was like her — breaking the prediction's grip. The chat goes silent forever. Emotional beat: belonging claimed, not earned.
